description.value: A large campground on Carp Lake in northern BC, accessed by gravel road and suited to fishing and flatwater paddling; remote from services with no confirmed facilities beyond basic camping.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record names this 'Kettle Bay Campground' with operator 'Quartz Contracting', but the linked website is the BC Parks page for Carp Lake Park, which mentions Kettle Bay only as a boating bay — not as a named campground. The website confirms 102 total campsites across the park (matching OSM capacity=102), states water and firewood are the only supplies available, notes the nearest settlement is 32km away, and prominently features a 'Book camping' button. OSM tags internet_access=no and power_supply=no are consistent with the website's characterization of facilities as 'rudimentary.'
concerns: Name mismatch: OSM names this 'Kettle Bay Campground' with operator 'Quartz Contracting', but the linked website is the official BC Parks page for 'Carp Lake Park'. 'Kettle Bay' appears in the website only as a bay where boaters are asked to reduce speed — it is not identified as a distinct campground name. The OSM record may represent one of the two unnamed campgrounds within the park, or a contractor-managed sub-facility not separately identified on the BC Parks site.

Operator 'Quartz Contracting' (northquartz@aol.com) is not mentioned anywhere on the BC Parks website, raising uncertainty about whether this is an independently operated site co-located within the park or a misattributed OSM record.
Phone number +1-250-964-3489 is not confirmed by the BC Parks website and likely belongs to the private contractor rather than BC Parks reservations.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A real, operating campground within a BC Parks unit, open year-round with 102 sites — clearly useful to touring cyclists navigating Northern BC's sparse settlement corridor.
enrichment_extras.notes: The OSM capacity of 102 exactly matches the website's stated total of '102 fully maintained campsites' across Carp Lake Park's two campgrounds, suggesting this OSM record may represent the entire park rather than an isolated campground named Kettle Bay.

wow_evidence: remote from services with no confirmed facilities beyond basic camping
